# ClipFlow

> ClipFlow is a free (beta) Chrome extension that saves web pages, highlighted text and Gmail emails straight into ClickUp tasks, Asana tasks or Airtable records. It is event-driven (no background CPU or polling), needs no Google OAuth for Gmail, and runs 100% locally with no ClipFlow server.

- Install: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/clipflow/djokbldinhahcmceginmgedppkpegnlk
- Website: https://broompositive.github.io/clipflow-site/
- Current version: 0.4.0 (free beta, every feature unlocked)
- Not affiliated with ClickUp, Asana, Airtable or Google.

## What it does
- Targets: ClickUp tasks, Asana tasks (workspace, project, section, assignee, due date, custom fields), Airtable records (any base/table, field mapping).
- Sources: any web page (title, URL, selection, meta description, CSS-selector values) and the Gmail email currently open (subject, sender, link, cleaned body).
- Reusable clip forms: set list/table, status, priority, tags, relative due date (e.g. +2d) and custom fields once; then clip in one click or Ctrl+Enter. Alt+Shift+C opens the popup.
- Template variables: {{title}} {{url}} {{selection}} {{metaDescription}} {{email.subject}} {{email.from}} {{email.url}} {{email.body}} {{date}} {{date+2d}} {{css.name}}
- Airtable on the Free plan: uses an Airtable Personal Access Token (scopes data.records:write, schema.bases:read).

## Performance and privacy model
- No background timers or polling; nothing runs between clips. The popup opens from a 5-minute local cache of workspace names.
- Nothing is injected on other sites except a small "Save to ClipFlow" button on Gmail; other pages are read only when the user opens the popup (activeTab).
- No servers, no telemetry, no tracking. Tokens, forms and cache live in chrome.storage.local. Clips go directly from the browser to api.clickup.com, app.asana.com or api.airtable.com using the user's own token.
- Gmail: reads only the open email from the page at click time; does not use the Gmail API or request Google OAuth.
